work_or_witness: Tactics Ogre: Reborn official Japanese product page · Character section, デニム・パウエル / Denim Powell profile
canonical_term: ウォルスタ解放軍 (Walister Liberation Army)
definition: The organization named in Denim's profile, whose members conduct guerrilla activity against Bakram and Galgastani forces.
cultural_caution: This is a fictional political-military organization in a branching game narrative, not a generic rebel, nationality, or character node.

citations.locator: Character section, デニム・パウエル / Denim Powell profile
supports: Denim is described as a member of the Walister Liberation Army undertaking guerrilla activity.

work_or_witness: Take a new look at Tactics Ogre: Reborn · Units and classes; The Battle System
definition: Square Enix calls the individuals composing Denam's order Units; they may be selected for battles, equipped, and developed.
cultural_caution: Unit is an interface and rules term. It must not collapse named characters into generic pieces or create a unit node in a character-only graph.

citations.locator: Units and classes; The Battle System
supports: The official article defines the order's individuals as Units and describes selection, equipment, and battle participation.

work_or_witness: Take a new look at Tactics Ogre: Reborn · Units and classes, paragraphs 1–3; Tactics Ogre: Reborn official Japanese product page · System: Battle Design Remade, Unit-by-unit level management
literal_gloss: ruleset with distinct abilities and level-up tendencies
definition: Units have classes with different abilities and different statistical tendencies on level-up; Square Enix's Japanese page says Reborn manages levels by unit rather than by class.
cultural_caution: A game class is not a character, caste, species, office, or direct equivalent of another setting's profession taxonomy.

supports: Classes have different abilities and different level-up tendencies.

citations.locator: System: Battle Design Remade, Unit-by-unit level management
supports: Reborn changes from the class-level management used in Tactics Ogre: Wheel of Fortune to unit-level management.

work_or_witness: Take a new look at Tactics Ogre: Reborn · Elements explained, paragraphs 1–3
definition: Reborn assigns one of eight elements—fire, water, wind, earth, darkness, light, lightning, or ice—to Denam and other units; matching magic or weapon elements increases power and affinities have strengths and weaknesses.
cultural_caution: The game calls these elements and connects Denam's selection to its fictional Xytegenia myth. They are game affinities, not cross-cultural natural philosophies or deity nodes.

supports: The eight elements, unit affinities, matching bonuses, and elemental strengths/weaknesses.

work_or_witness: Take a new look at Tactics Ogre: Reborn · The Battle System, paragraphs 5–7
literal_gloss: turn-order system based on Recovery Time
definition: The English official overview says battles are not turn-based; units take turns according to the RT system, with an acting turn called AT (Attack Turn).
cultural_caution: RT and AT are implementation rules, not temporal, ritual, or metaphysical claims about the setting.

supports: Battles use the RT system and designate an acting turn as AT.

work_or_witness: Take a new look at Tactics Ogre: Reborn · A branching narrative with multiple endings, paragraphs 1–2
definition: Reborn's story developments and conclusion can change with player decisions; the official article says allies may fracture into friend and foe according to ideology.
cultural_caution: Branching routes prevent presentation of a single universal relationship graph. Route-specific claims need their own scene and path evidence.

citations.locator: A branching narrative with multiple endings, paragraphs 1–2
supports: Player decisions can change developments and endings, including alliances that fracture by ideology.

work_or_witness: Take a new look at Tactics Ogre: Reborn · Tarot Cards and Character Creation, paragraphs 1–3
canonical_term: タロットカード / Tarot Cards
definition: During character creation, questions posed through the 22 major arcana determine Denam's initial parameters/statistics.
cultural_caution: Tarot is used here as a fictional game-character-creation device. It must not be represented as a claim about real divinatory practice or fate.

citations.locator: Tarot Cards and Character Creation, paragraphs 1–3
supports: Major-arcana answers determine the protagonist's initial stats.

work_or_witness: Tactics Ogre: Reborn official Japanese product page · Character section, Lanselot Hamilton, Mirdyn Walhorn, and Gildas W. Byrne profiles
definition: The official character profiles identify Lanselot as its former commander and Mirdyn and Gildas as former members.
cultural_caution: This fictional organization is an affiliation attribute, not a person, job class, historical knightly order, or graph endpoint.

citations.locator: Character section, Lanselot Hamilton, Mirdyn Walhorn, and Gildas W. Byrne profiles
supports: The profiles identify their former Holy Knights of New Xenobia roles.

work_or_witness: Tactics Ogre: Reborn official Japanese product page · Character section, カノープス・ウォルフ / Canopus Wolph profile
definition: The Canopus profile calls him a Xenobian 有翼人 and distinguishes the group's lifespan from that of ordinary people.
cultural_caution: This setting-specific designation describes Canopus in the selected witness; it must not be converted into a universal race/species node or compared as an exact equivalence across settings.

supports: The profile identifies Canopus as 有翼人 and describes the group's lifespan distinction.
